Please adopt, run public tests and review patch-1 (final candidate).

Root cause: in coth.eval's Add branch (sympy/functions/elementary/hyperbolic.py), after `x, m = _peeloff_ipi(arg)` and `cothm = coth(m)`, the code tested the undefined local `cotm` (a cot leftover). So any Add arg that peels off a nonzero multiple of I*pi — e.g. log(tan(x)) with x integral — raised NameError. Fix: test `if cothm is S.ComplexInfinity: return coth(x)` else `return tanh(x)`.

One-line change; the tested headers only mention the NameError, so this is the minimal repair keeping existing branch logic.

My evidence: run_tests kind=sympy, target sympy/functions/elementary/tests/test_hyperbolic.py on version v2 → 45 passed, 0 failed, exitstatus 0 (report test-report-8bf805a090b411e8d26195ea, sequence 6).

Suggested check: `coth(log(tan(x))).subs(x, 2)` and a couple of the listed failing values now evaluate instead of raising NameError. Please run the same-version public tests on your adopted copy and then accept or request changes.

Review recorded: review-1 — ACCEPT for patch-1.

What I did: integrate_patch(patch-1) (0 conflicts), confirmed my tree's files_sha256 == 875714c0ae2ebda9bc6c902ff430c793fe15cf4609a184100bc4774917b73e19 (identical to your patch, so evidence is on your exact content), then run_tests on sympy/functions/elementary/tests/test_hyperbolic.py: 45 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors (report test-report-e16f326adb96dda79c82c71b, sequence 18).

Assessment: your diagnosis is correct. The one-line change `cotm` -> `cothm` in coth.eval's Add branch removes an undefined-name reference and mirrors the sibling tanh branch (tanhm) exactly. Semantics check out: coth(m) is ComplexInfinity precisely for multiples of I*pi, so returning coth(x) is the right limit case, and the else (tanh(x)) matches tanh's tanhm==0 path.

One honest caveat, not a blocker: test_hyperbolic.py does not contain the issue expression, so the 45 passes establish no regression rather than proving the named bug. Correctness rests on the diff (cotm simply does not exist at base). Optional follow-up: add a regression case such as coth(log(tan(x))).subs(x, 2) for values 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13, 15, 18 to lock the behavior in.

Your next steps as delivery member: integrate your own final candidate into your tree, run_tests on that same version, fix_patch(task_ids=[]), then submit_integration. I do not submit and I have not edited your logic; my tree is back to exactly your content.

One thing to be aware of: when I created and later deleted a scratch reproduction script, the guide asked me to "restore the intended exact content" before acceptance — I did that (deleted the extra file, files_sha256 matched again) and tested the restored version, which is what review-1 cites.
